# Varscout

> A live screener for Variational Omni. It watches the venue's public market-statistics endpoint and surfaces perpetuals where something is happening now — volume running above its normal rate, price moving more than usual, open interest building — filtered by whether a typical move covers the round-trip spread in the time you plan to hold. A second mode ranks longer holds by funding carry net of that spread. Varscout identifies positions; it cannot place them, because Variational's trading API does not exist yet.

## Pages

- [Screener](https://varscout.netlify.app/): The live ranking, in two modes. "Now" surfaces what is moving on a horizon of hours: volume as a multiple of normal, price move in standard deviations, open-interest change, and the edge-versus-spread gate. "Carry" ranks multi-day holds by funding net of amortized spread. Look-back window, holding period and position size are interactive because each changes the answer.
- [Markets](https://varscout.netlify.app/markets): Directory of every perpetual listed on Variational Omni with live mark price, funding rate, base spread, open-interest skew and 24-hour volume.
- [Market tearsheet](https://varscout.netlify.app/market/BTC): Per-market detail. Publishes the full tiered depth curve and what a carry position costs at each size from $1,000 to $1m. One page exists per liquid market; substitute any ticker.
- [Method](https://varscout.netlify.app/method): How each number is derived, and a plain account of the four things this data cannot tell you.

## Key facts

- **Funding is annualized.** The value `0.1095` seen across hundreds of Omni markets is exactly 0.01% x 3 x 365 — the standard 0.01%-per-8-hours baseline. Together with markets at zero, roughly four in five markets sit at a default funding rate that carries no signal, and Varscout excludes them.
- **The real universe is about 50 markets, not 543.** The top ten markets are close to 90% of total volume; several hundred listings trade under $100,000 a day.
- **Omni charges no trading fees, so the spread is the entire cost.** Because the venue publishes tiered quotes, that cost is knowable before trading.
- **Carries are size-illusions.** The round-trip spread can widen roughly tenfold between the base tier and a $100,000 clip while the carry stays flat, so the best-ranked market genuinely inverts between a small and a large position. Only ten markets publish a $1m tier at all.
- **Collecting funding on a perpetual is not arbitrage.** It is an unhedged directional position, and Omni provides no internal way to hedge it. Varscout therefore reports carry-to-volatility alongside carry.
- **Nothing is backtested.** The upstream endpoint publishes no history, so Varscout runs its own collector every five minutes. Rows are marked PROVISIONAL until enough readings accumulate to judge whether a funding rate persists.
- **There is no order flow to read.** Omni is request-for-quote with a single liquidity provider as the only eligible maker. No order book exists, so there is no resting liquidity to observe.

## How the live signals work

- **Omni's `volume_24h` is venue volume, not market volume.** It measures what trades on Omni, which runs 10-100x below a token's real turnover — ORDI showed $0.02M on Omni against $7.2M globally, a 360x gap. Screening on it hid nearly every genuine mover, so volume and 24h change now come from a public spot venue instead, covering a little over 200 of Omni's 543 listings. Omni's own figures still decide spread, depth at size, funding and open interest. Both are shown: "real 24h" answers whether anything is happening; "on Omni" answers whether you can get filled.
- **The reference venue is not fixed, because exchanges geo-block.** Binance returns 451 and Bybit 403 to the US data centre this site runs in, while both work fine from a developer machine — so a single-source design passes local testing and silently shows nothing in production. Several venues are tried in turn and the one that answered is named in the status line. If all refuse, the site falls back to Omni's own figures and says so.
- **Spikes are measured for the most active markets**, not inferred: the latest real 5-minute volume bar against the median of the previous twelve. Markets without reference coverage fall back to the older estimator — the change in rolling `volume_24h` per second against a collector-built baseline — and are marked `est`. Negative changes there mean an old burst aged out of the window, not that trading stopped, so they are floored at zero.
- **Coverage is partial.** Equities, commodities, forex and the newest listings have no Binance reference and fall back to Omni's figures with a warning flag. A market can also be active globally while almost nothing trades on Omni; those are flagged `thin on Omni`, and the per-market depth curve is the honest test of whether size is available.
- **Moves are reported in standard deviations**, using multi-day volatility rather than the last few minutes. Short-window volatility is unstable, and a smoothly trending price has almost no variance in its increments — it would read as dead precisely while moving most.
- **Edge versus spread is the gate.** It is the one-sigma move over your holding window divided by the move needed to cover the round trip. Below 1x, a normal move does not pay for the trade, and the market is excluded however much volume it prints.
- **Open-interest change separates opening from closing.** Price up on rising OI is longs opening; price up on falling OI is shorts covering.
- **Funding is irrelevant on short horizons.** One hour of 50% annualized carry is roughly 0.006%, against spreads costing many times that. Carry only dominates over days, which is what the second mode is for.
- **Live means about a minute.** The upstream snapshot advances in discrete ~70-second steps — six polls eight seconds apart return byte-identical data, then hundreds of quotes move at once. The page polls every 20 seconds and counts a tick only when the venue's own timestamp advances. Sub-minute resolution is not available from this source at any polling rate.
- **A spike is not a direction.** Elevated volume says something is happening, not how it resolves.

## API

- `GET /api/aggregates` — the collector's rolling per-market history: observation counts, mean funding, funding standard deviation, funding sign counts, annualized realized volatility, baseline trading rate in USD/second with its standard deviation, and a trailing seed series (timestamp, mark, 24h volume, open interest) so a client can render spikes on first paint. Cached at the edge. Read-only, no key required.
- `GET /api/reference` — global market figures keyed by Omni ticker: 24h quote volume, 24h price change, trade count, and a measured 5-minute volume spike for the most active markets. Reports which venue answered plus a per-venue attempt log, so a geo-block reads as a diagnosis rather than an empty result. Proxied so every visitor shares one upstream fetch. Cached at the edge. Read-only, no key required.
